text.p: France unveiled a new 200-franc banknote on Friday, part of its plans to replace older bills in an attempt to curtail counterfeiting.
The new bill has a picture of French inventor Gustave Eiffel with part of his most famous creation -- the Eiffel Tower -- in the background.
Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet told a news conference Eiffel was a perfect choice for the new banknote.

"He was a man with a worldwide reputation. He not only built superb works in France, the Eiffel Tower being the best known, but also the metallic internal architecture of the Statue of Liberty in New York," he said.
The 200 franc bill is the third in the new series of franc notes bearing pictures of famous French men and women.
It was preceded by a 50-franc bill, with a picture of writer Antoine de Saint Exupery and a 500-franc bill adorned by French scientists Pierre and Marie Curie.
A 100-franc bill to be launched next year will carry the image of post-Impressionist painter Paul Cezanne.
Trichet said the new banknotes would be very difficult to falsify because of eight security markings specifically aimed at making counterfeiting more difficult.
The eight measures include colour shifting markings, micro and mini-lettering, filigree and metal wire.
